# LiveKit telemetry semantic conventions

The attribute keys, events and spans LiveKit producers send over OTLP, and what they mean.
Schema `https://livekit.io/schemas/telemetry/0.3.0`, stability `development`. Built on
[OpenTelemetry semantic conventions v1.44.0](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/tree/v1.44.0):
OTel keys are used as OTel defines them and are not redefined here.

Generated from `otel/model` in livekit/protocol; change the model, not this file. It registers
the keys shared across producers and what the LiveKit client SDKs send today (the Rust core
behind the native SDKs, and the JS port). How and when telemetry is sent (transport, cadence,
batching, retries, storage) is not part of the conventions.

Contents: [Conventions](#conventions) · [Resource](#resource) · [Every record](#every-record) ·
[Plain log records](#plain-log-records) · [Events](#events) · [Spans](#spans) ·
[Attribute reference](#attribute-reference) · [Enum values](#enum-values) · [Bindings](#bindings)

## Conventions

**OTel first.** OTel defines the record model (timestamp, severity, trace and span ids, span
status, `service.name`) and the keys LiveKit reuses (`service.*`, `os.*`, `device.*`,
`network.connection.type`, `error.type`, `session.id`, `code.*`, `telemetry.sdk.*`). LiveKit keys
carry the `lk.` prefix. Requirement levels have their OTel meaning; a conditional requirement's
condition is prose.

**Ownership.** `shared` keys are concepts several producers send; changing one needs Client,
Agents and Observability review. `client` keys belong to the Client team. Every LiveKit key's
owner is in the [attribute reference](#attribute-reference).

**Flat shared identity.** Shared identity keys are flat, `lk.<entity>_<field>`, never
`lk.<entity>.sid`:
`lk.job_id`, `lk.participant_id`, `lk.room_sid`, `lk.track_sid`.
They are record and span attributes, never Resource attributes, omitted until the server has
assigned them, and never default metric dimensions (high cardinality).

**PII.** Customer-supplied values go under `lk.pii.*`. The `pii` key segment is the collector's
redaction contract: with redaction on, it deletes every attribute whose key has a `pii` segment and
keeps everything else. Log bodies and metrics are never redacted, so PII must not go there.
PII keys: `lk.pii.participant_identity`, `lk.pii.remote_participant_identity`, `lk.pii.room_name`.

**Units.** Durations are seconds (OTel), on a monotonic clock; timestamps are the record's own
OTLP time. One documented exception: RTC stats keep the W3C webrtc-stats milliseconds, in keys
ending in `_ms`:
`lk.rtc.freezes_duration_ms`, `lk.rtc.interruptions_duration_ms`, `lk.rtc.jitter_buffer_delay_ms`, `lk.rtc.jitter_ms.avg`, `lk.rtc.jitter_ms.max`, `lk.rtc.jitter_ms.min`, `lk.rtc.pauses_duration_ms`, `lk.rtc.quality_limitation.bandwidth_ms`, `lk.rtc.quality_limitation.cpu_ms`, `lk.rtc.quality_limitation.other_ms`, `lk.rtc.rtt_ms.avg`, `lk.rtc.rtt_ms.max`, `lk.rtc.rtt_ms.min`, `lk.rtc.window_ms`.

**Keys the SDK owns.** Apps never set these, on their own events or as session attributes:
prefixes `lk.`, `otel.`, `code.` and keys
`session.id`, `error.type`.

**App events.** An app's events are named `custom.<name>` (see [`custom`](#custom)), so they never
collide with or spoof LiveKit events, and stay within these limits:
attributes per event 64, attributes per session 64, key bytes 128, name bytes 128, string value bytes 1024.
Anything over a limit is rejected, never truncated, and counted in `lk.telemetry.dropped.invalid`.

**Records.** An event is an OTLP log record with `event_name`; its severity and body are listed
with it. The JS port sends every event's name as its body. A record's timestamp and attributes are
taken when it is captured. Every record and span of a room session carries the
[session attributes](#every-record).

**Spans.** A span is one attempt at an operation; the session is the trace. LiveKit span names are
verbs, never ids. Span status is `Unset` on success and on cancellation, `Error` on failure.
`lk.outcome` (`ok`, `error`, `cancelled`) is on every span exactly once, and rollups read it, never
the status. `error.type` is a type name, never a message, at most 128 bytes, present only when the
span failed with a type. The core writes both; a span attribute of either name set any other way is
dropped. Checkpoints are span events without attributes, named from a fixed list per span. Past a
span's limits, later checkpoints are dropped and counted in OTLP `dropped_events_count`; app
correlation attributes are dropped first, then the span's own tail, counted in
`dropped_attributes_count`; the session's attributes, `lk.outcome` and `error.type` always ship.

## Resource

Resource attributes of the client pipeline, one Resource per process. Set once per pipeline. Session-specific keys (`lk.room_sid`, `lk.participant_id`, `lk.track_sid`) never go here; they stay on records and spans.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `service.name` | string | Required | Logical name of the service. `livekit-client-<sdk>`: swift, android, flutter, react-native, unity, rust, js; `livekit-client` when the platform names none. Set by the platform SDK. |
| `service.version` | string | Required | The version string of the service component. The format is not defined by these conventions. The LiveKit client SDK's version. Set by the platform SDK. |
| `telemetry.sdk.language` | enum | Required | The language of the telemetry SDK. `rust` from the Rust core (every native SDK), `webjs` from the JS port. |
| `telemetry.sdk.name` | string | Required | The name of the telemetry SDK as defined above. The telemetry library, `livekit-telemetry`, in every client. |
| `telemetry.sdk.version` | string | Required | The version string of the telemetry SDK. The telemetry library's version (the JS port sends `0.1.0`). |
| `browser.name` | string | Conditionally required: The JS SDK running in a browser. | Browser name. Resource attribute, JS port only. |
| `browser.version` | string | Conditionally required: The JS SDK running in a browser. | Browser version. Resource attribute, JS port only. |
| `device.model.identifier` | string | Recommended | The model identifier for the device. Set by the platform SDK where it knows the model; the JS port only when a host SDK supplies it. |
| `lk.sdk.name` | string | Recommended | LiveKit SDK name. Resource attribute. A low-cardinality metric dimension. Matches the `<sdk>` part of `service.name = livekit-client-<sdk>`. |
| `lk.sdk.version` | string | Recommended | LiveKit SDK version. Resource attribute. A low-cardinality metric dimension. |
| `os.name` | string | Recommended | Human readable operating system name. Set by the platform SDK; the JS port only when a host SDK supplies it. |
| `os.version` | string | Recommended | The version string of the operating system as defined in [Version Attributes](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/resource/README.md#version-attributes). Set by the platform SDK; the JS port only when a host SDK supplies it. |

## Every record

Attributes the core stamps on every log record and span of a session. One session is one Room connection lifetime, across reconnects, and one trace. A record's attributes and timestamp are taken when it is captured, the session's included, so a record captured before a disconnect keeps its room. Records outside a room (device state, pre-room errors, self-telemetry) belong to the process's own session and carry only `session.id`. Keys the SDK owns (`lk.*`, `otel.*`, `code.*`, `session.id`, `error.type`) are never set by an app; an app's correlation attributes (e.g. `app.call_id`, `enduser.id`) ride along, within the `custom` event's limits.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session.id` | string | Required | A unique ID to identify a session. The session's trace id (32 hex characters), also on the process's own records. |
| `lk.participant_id` | string | Conditionally required: Once the client has joined the room. | Server-assigned SID of the local participant (`PA_...`). On every record and span of a session once the client has joined. High cardinality, never a default metric dimension. |
| `lk.pii.participant_identity` | string | Conditionally required: Once the client has joined the room. | Customer-supplied identity of the local participant. On every record and span of a session once the client has joined. |
| `lk.pii.room_name` | string | Conditionally required: Once the client has joined the room. | Customer-supplied room name. On every record and span of a session once the client has joined. |
| `lk.room_sid` | string | Conditionally required: Once the client has joined the room. | Server-assigned room session SID (`RM_...`). On every record and span of a session once the client has joined; absent before join. High cardinality, never a default metric dimension. |
| `otel.event.name` | string | Conditionally required: On event records; duplicates the record's `event_name`. | Identifies the class / type of event. For backends that do not surface the OTLP `event_name` field yet. |

## Plain log records

Attributes of a plain log record (no event name). The body is the log message. Only WARN and ERROR records are sent; WebRTC lines only at ERROR, and the telemetry module's own lines never. In records the core copies from Rust (`lk.log.source = ffi`), JWT-shaped substrings are masked as `<jwt>`.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.log.logger` | string | Required | Logger, type, module or file that wrote the line. Free text from the platform's logger. |
| `lk.log.source` | enum | Required | Which layer wrote the log line. Only WARN and ERROR records are sent; WebRTC lines only at ERROR. |
| `code.file.path` | string | Recommended | The source code filename that identifies the code unit as uniquely as possible (preferably an absolute file path). This attribute MUST NOT be used on the Profile signal since the data is already captured in 'message Function'. This constraint is imposed to prevent redundancy and maintain data integrity. The source file that logged the line. |
| `code.function.name` | string | Recommended | The method or function fully-qualified name without arguments. The value should fit the natural representation of the language runtime, which is also likely the same used within `code.stacktrace` attribute value. This attribute MUST NOT be used on the Profile signal since the data is already captured in 'message Function'. This constraint is imposed to prevent redundancy and maintain data integrity. The function that logged the line, as the platform names it. |
| `code.line.number` | int | Recommended | The line number in `code.file.path` best representing the operation. It SHOULD point within the code unit named in `code.function.name`. This attribute MUST NOT be used on the Profile signal since the data is already captured in 'message Line'. This constraint is imposed to prevent redundancy and maintain data integrity. The line in `code.file.path`. |

## Events

### `custom`

Namespace of app-defined events. The core emits `custom.<name>` with the app's own attributes. The `custom.` prefix keeps app events from colliding with or spoofing `lk.*` events. An app's attributes, on its events and on the session (correlation attributes such as `app.call_id`), may not use the reserved keys, and stay within the limits; anything else is rejected, never truncated, and counted in `lk.telemetry.dropped.invalid`. An event's own attributes override the session's.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: The event name (`custom.<name>`).

### `lk.device.app_state.changed`

The app moved to the foreground or background. Sent once with the initial state, then on each change. All platforms.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `app: background` (Rust core); the event name (JS port).

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.device.app_state` | enum | Required | Whether the app is in front of the user. All platforms; the web maps page visibility. |

### `lk.device.audio.interruption`

An audio session interruption began or ended. iOS; Android from audio focus loss and gain. Not sent by the JS port.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `audio interruption began`.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.device.audio.interruption` | enum | Required | Phase of an audio session interruption. iOS audio session interruptions; Android audio focus loss and gain. |

### `lk.device.audio_route.changed`

The audio route changed. iOS; Android from its audio device callbacks; optional elsewhere. Not sent by the JS port.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `audio route: speaker (old_device_unavailable)`.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.device.audio_route.outputs` | string | Required | The active outputs, comma-separated. Each item is one of speaker, receiver, wired_headset, bluetooth, car_audio, air_play, hdmi, usb, other. A string, not an array: the vocabulary is closed but the list is joined. |
| `lk.device.audio_route.reason` | enum | Required | Why the audio route changed. AVAudioSession route change reasons on iOS; Android maps its audio device callbacks; `unknown` where the platform gives none. |

### `lk.device.battery.changed`

Charging changed, or the level crossed 20 % or 10 % unplugged. Never per percent; silent where the level is unknown. iOS and Android; not sent by the JS port.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `battery: 18%` or `battery: 64%, charging`.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.device.battery.charging` | boolean | Required | The device is charging. Sent together with `lk.device.battery.level`. |
| `lk.device.battery.level` | int, `%` | Required | Battery charge in percent, 0-100. Only where the level is known (iOS, Android; not desktops or tvOS); never from the JS port. An integer percentage, not a 0-1 ratio. |

### `lk.device.capture.failed`

A capture device failed. All platforms.

- Severity: `WARN`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `capture failed: camera (permission_denied)` (Rust core); the event name (JS port).

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.device.capture.device` | enum | Required | Capture device that failed. All platforms. |
| `lk.device.capture.reason` | enum | Required | Why capture failed, in the getUserMedia failure taxonomy. iOS: authorization status and capture interruptions; Android: permission checks and camera callbacks; web: DOMException names. |

### `lk.device.low_power.changed`

Low Power Mode changed. Sent once with the initial reading, then on each change; never where the platform has no source.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `low power mode: on` (Rust core); the event name (JS port).

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.device.low_power.enabled` | boolean | Required | Low Power Mode / Battery Saver is on. Absent where the platform has no source. iOS, macOS and Android; optional elsewhere. |

### `lk.device.memory.changed`

Memory pressure changed. Sent once with the initial reading, then on each change.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `memory pressure: warning` (Rust core); the event name (JS port).

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.device.memory.pressure` | enum | Required | Memory pressure as the OS reports it. Apple `DispatchSource` memory-pressure levels; Android `onTrimMemory`: RUNNING_LOW and BACKGROUND map to `warning`, RUNNING_CRITICAL and COMPLETE to `critical`. iOS, macOS and Android; optional elsewhere. |

### `lk.device.network.changed`

The network path changed. Sent once with the initial state, then when any of its attributes changes. All platforms. A platform that cannot read the connection's details (a browser without the Network Information API) sends only `network.connection.type`, as `unknown` or `unavailable`.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `network: cell, expensive` (Rust core); the event name (JS port).

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `network.connection.type` | enum | Required | The internet connection type. Clients also send `vpn`, `bluetooth` and `other`, which are not OTel members; `unknown` when the platform cannot tell, `unavailable` when offline. |
| `lk.device.network.constrained` | boolean | Conditionally required: When the platform reports it. | The user asked for less traffic (Low Data Mode, Data Saver). Apple `NWPath.isConstrained`, Android Data Saver; on the web `navigator.connection.saveData`, only where the Network Information API exists. |
| `lk.device.network.expensive` | boolean | Conditionally required: When the platform reports it. | The network is metered (cellular, personal hotspot). Apple `NWPath.isExpensive`, Android metered networks; on the web only where the Network Information API exists. |

### `lk.device.thermal.changed`

Thermal state changed. Sent once with the initial reading, then on each change. A platform without a thermal source sends none. A device event: a record of the process, not of a room session.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `thermal: serious` (Rust core); the event name (JS port).

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.device.thermal.state` | enum | Required | Thermal pressure as the OS reports it. Apple `ProcessInfo.thermalState`, Android `PowerManager` thermal status, web Compute Pressure API, all mapped to this vocabulary. The platform's `unknown` (no thermal source) is no reading and is never emitted. iOS, macOS and Android; optional elsewhere. |

### `lk.ping`

Pipeline smoke test. Never emitted in production paths. Not sent by the JS port.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: The event name.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.ping.seq` | int | Recommended | Monotonically increasing sequence number per pipeline. Optional; on `lk.ping` only. |

### `lk.room.disconnected`

The Room left connected for good. Once per session, never on a reconnect. INFO when the client hung up (`client_initiated`), WARN otherwise.

- Severity: `INFO` or `WARN`
- Body: Display line, e.g. `disconnected: client_initiated` (Rust core); the event name (JS port).

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.disconnect.reason` | enum | Required | Why the session ended. The protocol's `DisconnectReason`, plus the client giving up (`reconnect_failed`). |

### `lk.rtc.stats.sample`

One RTC stats window for one track and direction. One per track and direction per window, timestamped at the window's end, also closed early when the track ends, at disconnect and at shutdown. Keyed by session and track: two rooms receiving the same track send two windows. Only the track, kind, direction, window and sample count are always present; counters and gauges a platform or direction lacks are omitted.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Display summary, e.g. `video inbound: 33 kbps, loss 0.0%, rtt 0 ms, 10 fps` (Rust core); the event name (JS port).

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.rtc.samples` | int, `{reading}` | Required | Stats readings folded into the window. Denominator for the gauges' averages. |
| `lk.rtc.window_ms` | int, `ms` | Required | Actual length of the stats window. From the window's start to its close, on the core's clock (the JS port uses wall-clock time). |
| `lk.track.direction` | enum | Required | Whether the stats describe sent or received media. On RTC stats windows only. |
| `lk.track.kind` | enum | Required | Media kind of the track. On publish and subscribe spans and RTC stats windows. |
| `lk.track_sid` | string | Required | Server-assigned track SID (`TR_...`). On publish and subscribe spans and RTC stats windows. A publish learns it only on success. High cardinality, never a default metric dimension. |
| `lk.rtc.audio_level.avg` | double, `1` | Conditionally required: Inbound audio. | Average audio level in the window, 0-1, inbound audio. Inbound `audioLevel`, averaged over `lk.rtc.samples` readings. |
| `lk.rtc.audio_level.max` | double, `1` | Conditionally required: Inbound audio. | Maximum audio level in the window, 0-1, inbound audio. Inbound `audioLevel`. |
| `lk.rtc.audio_level.min` | double, `1` | Conditionally required: Inbound audio. | Minimum audio level in the window, 0-1, inbound audio. Inbound `audioLevel`. |
| `lk.rtc.bytes` | int, `By` | Conditionally required: When the stats report it. | Bytes sent or received (cumulative). Outbound `bytesSent`, inbound `bytesReceived`. |
| `lk.rtc.codec` | string | Conditionally required: When known. | Codec mimeType, when known. The `codec` stats entry the RTP stream's `codecId` names. |
| `lk.rtc.concealed_samples` | int, `{sample}` | Conditionally required: Inbound audio. | Concealed audio samples, inbound audio (cumulative). Inbound `concealedSamples`. |
| `lk.rtc.concealment_events` | int, `{event}` | Conditionally required: Inbound audio. | Concealment events, inbound audio (cumulative). Inbound `concealmentEvents`. |
| `lk.rtc.fps.avg` | double, `{frame}/s` | Conditionally required: Video. | Average frame rate in the window, video. `framesPerSecond`, either direction, averaged over `lk.rtc.samples` readings. |
| `lk.rtc.fps.max` | double, `{frame}/s` | Conditionally required: Video. | Maximum frame rate in the window, video. `framesPerSecond`, either direction. |
| `lk.rtc.fps.min` | double, `{frame}/s` | Conditionally required: Video. | Minimum frame rate in the window, video. `framesPerSecond`, either direction. |
| `lk.rtc.freeze_count` | int, `{freeze}` | Conditionally required: Inbound video. | Video freezes, inbound video (cumulative). Inbound `freezeCount`. |
| `lk.rtc.freezes_duration_ms` | int, `ms` | Conditionally required: Inbound video. | Total freeze time, inbound video (cumulative). Inbound `totalFreezesDuration`. |
| `lk.rtc.interruption_count` | int, `{interruption}` | Conditionally required: Inbound audio. | Audio interruptions, inbound audio (cumulative). Inbound `interruptionCount`. |
| `lk.rtc.interruptions_duration_ms` | int, `ms` | Conditionally required: Inbound audio. | Total interruption time, inbound audio (cumulative). Inbound `totalInterruptionDuration`. |
| `lk.rtc.jitter_buffer_delay_ms` | int, `ms` | Conditionally required: Inbound. | Jitter buffer delay, inbound (cumulative). Inbound `jitterBufferDelay`. Average delay = jitter_buffer_delay_ms / jitter_buffer_emitted_count. |
| `lk.rtc.jitter_buffer_emitted_count` | int, `{sample}` | Conditionally required: Inbound. | Samples or frames emitted by the jitter buffer, inbound (cumulative). Inbound `jitterBufferEmittedCount`. |
| `lk.rtc.jitter_ms.avg` | double, `ms` | Conditionally required: Inbound. | Average jitter in the window, inbound. Inbound `jitter` (seconds × 1000), averaged over `lk.rtc.samples` readings. |
| `lk.rtc.jitter_ms.max` | double, `ms` | Conditionally required: Inbound. | Maximum jitter in the window, inbound. Inbound `jitter` (seconds × 1000). |
| `lk.rtc.jitter_ms.min` | double, `ms` | Conditionally required: Inbound. | Minimum jitter in the window, inbound. Inbound `jitter` (seconds × 1000). |
| `lk.rtc.packets` | int, `{packet}` | Conditionally required: When the stats report it. | Packets sent or received (cumulative). Outbound `packetsSent`, inbound `packetsReceived`. |
| `lk.rtc.packets_lost` | int, `{packet}` | Conditionally required: Inbound. | Packets lost, inbound (cumulative). Inbound `packetsLost`. Loss ratio = packets_lost / (packets + packets_lost). |
| `lk.rtc.pause_count` | int, `{pause}` | Conditionally required: Inbound video. | Video pauses, inbound video (cumulative). Inbound `pauseCount`. |
| `lk.rtc.pauses_duration_ms` | int, `ms` | Conditionally required: Inbound video. | Total pause time, inbound video (cumulative). Inbound `totalPausesDuration`. |
| `lk.rtc.quality_limitation.bandwidth_ms` | int, `ms` | Conditionally required: Outbound video. | Time the encoder was limited by bandwidth, outbound video (cumulative). Outbound `qualityLimitationDurations.bandwidth`. |
| `lk.rtc.quality_limitation.cpu_ms` | int, `ms` | Conditionally required: Outbound video. | Time the encoder was limited by CPU, outbound video (cumulative). Outbound `qualityLimitationDurations.cpu`. |
| `lk.rtc.quality_limitation.other_ms` | int, `ms` | Conditionally required: Outbound video. | Time the encoder was limited for other reasons, outbound video (cumulative). Outbound `qualityLimitationDurations.other`. |
| `lk.rtc.rtt_ms.avg` | double, `ms` | Conditionally required: When the window has readings. | Average round-trip time in the window. Same sources as `lk.rtc.rtt_ms.min`, averaged over `lk.rtc.samples` readings. |
| `lk.rtc.rtt_ms.max` | double, `ms` | Conditionally required: When the window has readings. | Maximum round-trip time in the window. Same sources as `lk.rtc.rtt_ms.min`. |
| `lk.rtc.rtt_ms.min` | double, `ms` | Conditionally required: When the window has readings. | Minimum round-trip time in the window. Outbound: the `remote-inbound-rtp` entry's `roundTripTime`; inbound: the nominated candidate pair's `currentRoundTripTime` (seconds × 1000). |
| `lk.rtc.silent_concealed_samples` | int, `{sample}` | Conditionally required: Inbound audio. | Concealed samples that were silent, inbound audio (cumulative). Inbound `silentConcealedSamples`. |

### `lk.telemetry.report`

Self-telemetry; counts since the previous report. Sent after a loss, failure, refusal, capped hold or disk error, and once at shutdown as the session summary, so fleet-wide success rates have denominators. A record of the process, not of a room session. Losses by policy (a project that receives nothing, the opt-out) are never reported.

- Severity: `INFO`
- Body: Rust core: a one-line summary, e.g. `telemetry: 4 batches sent (20480 B), 0 failed, 0 dropped, 0 cached`. JS port: the event name.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.telemetry.cache.batches` | int, `{batch}` | Required | Batches waiting in the cache now. A gauge, not a count since the previous report. Always present on a report. |
| `lk.telemetry.uploads.bytes` | int, `By` | Required | Compressed bytes the collector accepted. What telemetry cost the uplink. Always present on a report, even when 0. |
| `lk.telemetry.uploads.failed` | int, `{attempt}` | Required | Upload attempts that failed transiently (no answer, 429, 5xx). Always present on a report, even when 0. |
| `lk.telemetry.uploads.sent` | int, `{batch}` | Required | Batches the collector accepted. Always present on a report, even when 0. |
| `lk.telemetry.cache.delete_errors` | int, `{batch}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero (JS port only). | Sent batches the cache could not delete; never sent twice from the same launch. Only when non-zero. JS port only. |
| `lk.telemetry.cache.list_errors` | int, `{attempt}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero (JS port only). | Times the cache could not be listed, so nothing was reconciled or sent. Only when non-zero. JS port only. |
| `lk.telemetry.cache.read_errors` | int, `{batch}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero (JS port only). | Cached batches that could not be read right now, kept for the next pass. Only when non-zero. JS port only. |
| `lk.telemetry.cache.write_errors` | int, `{batch}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Batches the disk refused, kept in memory instead. Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.cache_error` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Records no cache, not even memory, could take. Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.cache_full` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Records evicted by the cache's size or file-count bound. Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.corrupt` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Records in cached batches that failed their CRC. Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.expired` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Records in batches past the cache's age limit. Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.invalid` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Custom events, attributes or SDK strings over the limits, rejected. Only when non-zero. Over-limit values are rejected, never truncated (a truncated id collides). |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.oversized` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Single records larger than the collector accepts (413). Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.queue_full` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Records evicted from the in-memory queue. Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.rate_limited` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Discrete events dropped by the flood guard. Only when non-zero. RTC stats windows and reports are exempt from the guard. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.rejected` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Records the collector rejected (final 4xx/5xx, OTLP partial success). Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.throttled` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero (Rust core only). | Records evicted from the cache during a server-directed pause. Only when non-zero. Rust core only; the JS port never sends it. |
| `lk.telemetry.dropped.unattributed` | int, `{record}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero (JS port only). | Log lines from a Room-shaped logging context with no telemetry scope behind it, dropped. Only when non-zero. JS port only. |
| `lk.telemetry.holds.capped` | int, `{hold}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Soft upload holds that reached their cap. Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.uploads.timeouts` | int, `{attempt}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | Upload attempts that hit the export timeout. Only when non-zero. |
| `lk.telemetry.uploads.unauthorized` | int, `{attempt}` | Conditionally required: When non-zero. | 401/403 answers (tokens the collector refused). Only when non-zero. |

## Spans

### `lk.connect`

Kind `client`. One connect attempt. Dashboards compute connect phases only from the required checkpoints, which every platform sends in this order; best-effort ones refine a platform's own view and may be missing or ordered differently.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.connect.attempt` | int | Required | 1-based connect attempt. 1 for the user-initiated connect; a platform that retries sets the next number on the next `lk.connect` span. |
| `lk.outcome` | enum | Required | How the attempt ended. Rollups read this, never the span status. Exactly once on every LiveKit span, written by the core from how the span ended; an attribute of this name set any other way is dropped. Status follows it: `Error` for `error`, `Unset` for `ok` and `cancelled`. |
| `error.type` | enum | Conditionally required: Only when `lk.outcome` is `error` and the failure has a type. | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. A type name, never a message, at most 128 bytes, platform-defined: Swift sends `LiveKitError.<numeric code>`, `CancellationError` or the Swift error type. Dashboards group by it per `service.name`. Written only by the core, at most once. |

| Checkpoint | Requirement | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ws_open` | Required | The signaling WebSocket opened. |
| `signal` | Required | Signaling is up (stamped with ws_open on the web and with join_recv on Swift). |
| `join_recv` | Required | The join response arrived. |
| `pc_created` | Required | The peer connections exist (stamped once the join is adopted). |
| `early_pc_created` | Best effort | A peer connection was created before the join response (JS port only). |
| `offer_sent` | Best effort | The publisher's SDP offer went out. |
| `answer_sent` | Best effort | The subscriber's SDP answer went out. |
| `engine` | Best effort | The RTC engine is ready (Swift stamps it with pc_connected). |
| `pc_connected` | Best effort | The primary peer connection connected. |
| `room_connected` | Best effort | The Room reached the connected state. |

Limits: 128 attributes, 128 span events per span.

### `lk.publish`

Kind `internal`. One track publish. A child of the ambient span when there is one; a publish before the connect completes (a microphone published early) is its own span in the session's trace.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.outcome` | enum | Required | How the attempt ended. Rollups read this, never the span status. Exactly once on every LiveKit span, written by the core from how the span ended; an attribute of this name set any other way is dropped. Status follows it: `Error` for `error`, `Unset` for `ok` and `cancelled`. |
| `lk.track.kind` | enum | Required | Media kind of the track. On publish and subscribe spans and RTC stats windows. |
| `lk.track.source` | enum | Required | Source of the track. The protocol's `TrackSource` in snake_case. Agents sends the FFI enum names instead (`lk.track_source = SOURCE_MICROPHONE`). |
| `error.type` | enum | Conditionally required: Only when `lk.outcome` is `error` and the failure has a type. | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. A type name, never a message, at most 128 bytes. Written only by the core, at most once. |
| `lk.track_sid` | string | Conditionally required: On success; the server assigns it. | Server-assigned track SID (`TR_...`). On publish and subscribe spans and RTC stats windows. A publish learns it only on success. High cardinality, never a default metric dimension. |

No checkpoints.

Limits: 128 attributes, 128 span events per span.

### `lk.reconnect`

Kind `client`. One reconnect cycle. `cancelled` when `disconnect()` or a newer reconnect wins. Each attempt is a checkpoint named `attempt <n> <mode>`, mirrored by `lk.reconnect.attempts` and `lk.reconnect.mode`.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.outcome` | enum | Required | How the attempt ended. Rollups read this, never the span status. Exactly once on every LiveKit span, written by the core from how the span ended; an attribute of this name set any other way is dropped. Status follows it: `Error` for `error`, `Unset` for `ok` and `cancelled`. |
| `lk.reconnect.reason` | enum | Required | What triggered the reconnect cycle. The protocol's `ReconnectReason` (`RR_*`), plus reasons only a client knows. |
| `error.type` | enum | Conditionally required: Only when `lk.outcome` is `error` and the failure has a type. | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. A type name, never a message, at most 128 bytes. Written only by the core, at most once. |
| `lk.reconnect.attempts` | int | Conditionally required: After the first attempt. | Reconnect attempts made in the cycle. Equals `<n>` of the last `attempt <n> <mode>` checkpoint. |
| `lk.reconnect.mode` | enum | Conditionally required: After the first attempt. | Mode of the last reconnect attempt. Updated with each `attempt <n> <mode>` checkpoint; matches the last one. |

| Checkpoint | Requirement | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attempt <n> <mode>` | One per attempt | One reconnect attempt; n counts from 1. Matches `^attempt [1-9][0-9]* (quick\|full)$`. |

Limits: 128 attributes, 128 span events per span.

### `lk.subscribe`

Kind `internal`. One subscription, from the intent to subscribe to the first media. Starts when the intent exists: a remote publish under autoSubscribe, a manual subscribe, or, for tracks already in the room, the join. Ends `ok` at the first inbound stats reading with bytes; `cancelled` on unsubscribe or unpublish before media; `error` on a subscription failure, or with `error.type = timed_out` when no media came within 30 s, also through a later disconnect. The core owns the span; an SDK only reports the remote track's lifecycle.

| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lk.outcome` | enum | Required | How the attempt ended. Rollups read this, never the span status. Exactly once on every LiveKit span, written by the core from how the span ended; an attribute of this name set any other way is dropped. Status follows it: `Error` for `error`, `Unset` for `ok` and `cancelled`. |
| `lk.track.kind` | enum | Required | Media kind of the track. On publish and subscribe spans and RTC stats windows. |
| `lk.track.source` | enum | Required | Source of the track. The protocol's `TrackSource` in snake_case. Agents sends the FFI enum names instead (`lk.track_source = SOURCE_MICROPHONE`). |
| `lk.track_sid` | string | Required | Server-assigned track SID (`TR_...`). On publish and subscribe spans and RTC stats windows. A publish learns it only on success. High cardinality, never a default metric dimension. |
| `error.type` | enum | Conditionally required: Only when `lk.outcome` is `error` and the failure has a type. | Describes a class of error the operation ended with. A type name, never a message, at most 128 bytes. `timed_out` when no media came within 30 s. |
| `lk.pii.remote_participant_identity` | string | Recommended | Customer-supplied identity of the remote participant a record is about (the publisher, on subscribe). On subscribe spans: the identity of the participant publishing the track. |

| Checkpoint | Requirement | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `subscribed` | Required | The platform reported the remote track subscribed. |
| `first_media` | Required | The first inbound stats reading with bytes; the span ends ok here. |

Limits: 128 attributes, 128 span events per span.

## Enum values

### `lk.device.app_state`

| Value | Meaning |

| `background` | In the background. |

### `lk.device.audio.interruption`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `began` | Interruption began (another app or a call took the audio session). |
| `ended` | Interruption ended. |

### `lk.device.audio_route.reason`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `new_device` | A new output became available. |
| `old_device_unavailable` | The previous output went away. |
| `category_change` | The audio session category changed. |
| `override` | The route was overridden. |
| `wake_from_sleep` | The device woke from sleep. |
| `no_suitable_route` | No route fits the category. |
| `route_configuration_change` | The route's configuration changed. |
| `unknown` | The platform gave no reason. |

### `lk.device.capture.device`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `camera` | Camera. |
| `microphone` | Microphone. |
| `screen_share` | Screen capture. |

### `lk.device.capture.reason`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `permission_denied` | The user or OS denied access. |
| `not_found` | No such device. |
| `in_use` | Another app holds the device. |
| `disconnected` | The device went away. |
| `other` | Anything else. |

### `lk.device.memory.pressure`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `normal` | No pressure. |
| `warning` | Low memory. |
| `critical` | Critically low memory. |

### `lk.device.thermal.state`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `nominal` | Within normal limits. |
| `fair` | Slightly elevated. |
| `serious` | High; the system reduces performance. |
| `critical` | Critical; the device needs to cool down. |

### `lk.disconnect.reason`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `client_initiated` | The client hung up (CLIENT_INITIATED). |
| `duplicate_identity` | Another participant joined with the same identity (DUPLICATE_IDENTITY). |
| `server_shutdown` | The server instance shut down (SERVER_SHUTDOWN). |
| `participant_removed` | RoomService.RemoveParticipant was called (PARTICIPANT_REMOVED). |
| `room_deleted` | RoomService.DeleteRoom was called (ROOM_DELETED). |
| `state_mismatch` | The server did not know the session the client tried to resume (STATE_MISMATCH). |
| `join_failure` | The client could not connect fully (JOIN_FAILURE). |
| `migration` | The server asked the participant to migrate (MIGRATION, Cloud only). |
| `signal_close` | The signal WebSocket closed unexpectedly (SIGNAL_CLOSE). |
| `room_closed` | The room closed after its participants left (ROOM_CLOSED). |
| `user_unavailable` | The SIP callee did not answer in time (USER_UNAVAILABLE). |
| `user_rejected` | The SIP callee rejected the call (USER_REJECTED). |
| `sip_trunk_failure` | SIP protocol failure (SIP_TRUNK_FAILURE). |
| `connection_timeout` | The server timed out the session (CONNECTION_TIMEOUT). |
| `media_failure` | Media failed or timed out (MEDIA_FAILURE). |
| `agent_error` | The agent failed (AGENT_ERROR). |
| `reconnect_failed` | The client ran out of reconnect attempts (client only). |
| `unknown` | UNKNOWN_REASON or a number the client does not know. |

### `lk.log.source`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sdk` | The platform SDK. |
| `ffi` | The Rust core, copied by the log forwarder with JWT-shaped substrings masked as `<jwt>`. |
| `webrtc` | WebRTC. |

### `lk.outcome`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ok` | Succeeded; span status Unset. |
| `error` | Failed; span status Error, with `error.type` when the failure has a type. |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled by the caller or superseded; span status Unset. |

### `lk.reconnect.mode`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `quick` | Resume the session (ICE restart). |
| `full` | Reconnect from scratch. |

### `lk.reconnect.reason`

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `signal_disconnected` | The signaling socket closed (RR_SIGNAL_DISCONNECTED). |
| `publisher_failed` | The publisher peer connection failed (RR_PUBLISHER_FAILED). |
| `subscriber_failed` | The subscriber peer connection failed (RR_SUBSCRIBER_FAILED). |
| `transport_failed` | A peer connection failed and the platform did not say which (client only). |
| `switch_candidate` | The server asked for a candidate switch (RR_SWITCH_CANDIDATE). |
| `network_changed` | The device moved to another network (client only). |
| `debug` | A test or a debug menu asked for it (client only). |
| `unknown` | RR_UNKNOWN or a number the client does not know. |
